name: Schtasks Creates or Changes a Task With a User-Writable or Every-Minute Interpreter Action (CAR-2021-12-001, tuned)
description:
Tuned implementation of the process branch of MITRE CAR-2021-12-001: schtasks.exe with /create or /change
whose task action is in a user-writable location, or that schedules a script interpreter / LOLBin every minute.
Case-insensitive by design - the Elastic query published with CAR-2021-12-001 matches "SCHTASKS" and "/CREATE"
case-sensitively and therefore misses the lower-case "schtasks.exe /Create" that Amadey and most tools use.
Companion of win_security_task_created_user_writable_car_2021_12_001.yml (Task Scheduler side).
query: any where (process.executable:"*\\schtasks.exe" or process.pe.original_file_name:"schtasks.exe") and (process.command_line like~ ("*/create*", "*/change*")) and (((process.command_line like~ ("*\\AppData\\*", "*\\Users\\Public\\*", "*\\ProgramData\\*", "*\\Temp\\*", "*%APPDATA%*", "*%LOCALAPPDATA%*", "*%TEMP%*", "*%PUBLIC%*", "*%ProgramData%*", "*\\Windows\\Tasks\\*", "*\\Windows\\PLA\\System*", "*\\Registration\\CRMLog*", "*\\FxsTmp*", "*\\spool\\drivers\\color*", "*\\tracing\\*")) and (not process.command_line:"*\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\*")) or process.command_line regex~ ".*c:\\\\users\\\\[^\\\\]+\\\\[^\\\\]+\\\\[^\\\\]+\\.exe.*" or (process.command_line regex~ ".*/sc[ ]+minute.*/mo[ ]+1([^0-9].*)?" and (process.command_line like~ ("*javascript*", "*powershell*", "*wmic*", "*rundll32*", "*cmd*", "*cscript*", "*wscript*", "*regsvr32*", "*mshta*", "*bitsadmin*", "*certutil*", "*msiexec*", "*javaw*"))))
author: Sayat Abdiraiym (AITU, Intro to Threat Hunting)
false_positives: Software installers that register per-user update tasks under AppData
note:
## Triage (CAR-2021-12-001, tuned for Amadey)

1. Read the task's action (`winlog.event_data.TaskContent` -> `<Command>` / `<Arguments>`, or the schtasks `/TR`).
   Is the program in AppData, Temp, Users\Public, ProgramData or directly in a user-profile folder?
2. Every-minute repetition (`PT1M`, `/SC MINUTE /MO 1`) + random lowercase name equal to the EXE name = Amadey pattern.
3. Hash the action's file and look it up (VirusTotal / MISP event #1); check its signer.
4. Pivot on the host: process tree of the creator (schtasks.exe parent, or no schtasks at all = API/COM),
   rundll32 `..., Main` plugins, outbound POST to `/<random>/index.php`.
5. Benign? Allow-list by task name + signer (per-user updaters under AppData), not by folder.

name: Scheduled Task Created or Changed With a User-Writable or Every-Minute Interpreter Action (CAR-2021-12-001, tuned)
description:
Tuned implementation of MITRE CAR-2021-12-001 on the Task Scheduler side (Security 4698 created / 4702 changed).
Fires when the task's action runs from a user-writable location (AppData, Temp, Users\Public, ProgramData,
Windows\Tasks, ...) or directly from a folder in the user profile (Amadey v5 on Windows 10/11:
C:\Users\<user>\<10 hex>\<name>.exe), or when a script interpreter / LOLBin is scheduled to repeat every minute.
Works whatever created the task (schtasks.exe, PowerShell cmdlets, the COM API), so it also sees Amadey v5,
which registers its task through COM without starting schtasks.exe.
Compared with the published analytic, the generic terms ".exe" and "cmd" alone are not enough (they match
almost every legitimate task); see week-07-mitre-car/04-evaluation-and-mapping.md.
query: any where (event.code like~ ("4698", "4702")) and (((winlog.event_data.TaskContent like~ ("*\\AppData\\*", "*\\Users\\Public\\*", "*\\ProgramData\\*", "*\\Temp\\*", "*%APPDATA%*", "*%LOCALAPPDATA%*", "*%TEMP%*", "*%PUBLIC%*", "*%ProgramData%*", "*\\Windows\\Tasks\\*", "*\\Windows\\PLA\\System*", "*\\Registration\\CRMLog*", "*\\FxsTmp*", "*\\spool\\drivers\\color*", "*\\tracing\\*")) and (not winlog.event_data.TaskContent:"*\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\*")) or winlog.event_data.TaskContent regex~ ".*c:\\\\users\\\\[^\\\\]+\\\\[^\\\\]+\\\\[^\\\\]+\\.exe.*" or (winlog.event_data.TaskContent:"*PT1M*" and (winlog.event_data.TaskContent like~ ("*javascript*", "*powershell*", "*wmic*", "*rundll32*", "*cmd*", "*cscript*", "*wscript*", "*regsvr32*", "*mshta*", "*bitsadmin*", "*certutil*", "*msiexec*", "*javaw*"))))
author: Sayat Abdiraiym (AITU, Intro to Threat Hunting)
false_positives: Per-user software updaters installed under AppData (e.g. some browser or chat clients) - allow-list by task name and signer
Admin scripts deliberately run from C:\ProgramData - allow-list by path
note:
## Triage (CAR-2021-12-001, tuned for Amadey)

1. Read the task's action (`winlog.event_data.TaskContent` -> `<Command>` / `<Arguments>`, or the schtasks `/TR`).
   Is the program in AppData, Temp, Users\Public, ProgramData or directly in a user-profile folder?
2. Every-minute repetition (`PT1M`, `/SC MINUTE /MO 1`) + random lowercase name equal to the EXE name = Amadey pattern.
3. Hash the action's file and look it up (VirusTotal / MISP event #1); check its signer.
4. Pivot on the host: process tree of the creator (schtasks.exe parent, or no schtasks at all = API/COM),
   rundll32 `..., Main` plugins, outbound POST to `/<random>/index.php`.
5. Benign? Allow-list by task name + signer (per-user updaters under AppData), not by folder.
